nvitk.gui.panels.statmodels.derived
===================================

.. py:module:: nvitk.gui.panels.statmodels.derived

.. autoapi-nested-parse::

   Derived-column editor.

   Description
   -----------
   Lets the analysis frame carry transformed measurements — ``log_pi``, a z-scored covariate, a ratio
   between two pipelines' measurements — as **real columns**. That matters because a formula-level
   transform (``log(pi) ~ …``) only exists inside patsy: it cannot be plotted, filtered on, or used as
   a mediation variable. A derived column can do all three.

   Three kinds:

   ``transform``   a canned function (:data:`~nvitk.stats.frame_ops.TRANSFORMS`) applied to one column
   ``expression``  a free-form expression over the frame's columns, e.g. ``pi / flow_mean``
   ``bins``        a continuous column cut into labelled groups — the ``tacsctot`` → ``tacsctot_group``
                   pattern, e.g. left carotid plaque volume into ``cp0`` (= 0), ``cp1`` (0–25],
                   ``cp2`` (25–100], ``cp3`` (> 100)

   Names are constrained to Python identifiers because
   :func:`~nvitk.stats.mixedlm.fit_or_load_mixedlm` sanitizes column names before fitting — a column
   called ``log(pi)`` would silently become ``log_pi_`` in the model frame and stop matching.

.. py:class:: DerivedColumnsDialog(parent: qtpy.QtWidgets.QWidget | None, *, frame: pandas.DataFrame, columns: Sequence[nvitk.stats.frame_ops.DerivedColumn] = (), bin_column: str | None = None)

   Bases: :py:obj:`qtpy.QtWidgets.QDialog`


   Add, edit, reorder and remove the frame's derived columns.

   The preview pane evaluates the whole list against the current frame every time it changes, so a
   broken expression or an out-of-domain transform is visible before the dialog is accepted.


   .. py:attribute:: _frame


   .. py:attribute:: _columns
      :type:  list[nvitk.stats.frame_ops.DerivedColumn]
      :value: []



   .. py:attribute:: _base_columns


   .. py:attribute:: _preview_frame


   .. py:method:: _build_list_side() -> qtpy.QtWidgets.QWidget

      Left column: the ordered list of derived columns plus its reorder/remove controls.



   .. py:method:: _build_editor_side() -> qtpy.QtWidgets.QWidget

      Right column: the definition form for a single derived column.



   .. py:method:: _build_merge_page() -> qtpy.QtWidgets.QWidget

      Pool the levels of a categorical column into fewer groups.

      The categorical counterpart of the bins page. Each level of the source column gets a text
      box holding the group it belongs to; levels sharing a group name are merged. Typing the
      same name in two boxes is the whole interface — there is no separate "create group" step,
      because the group *is* its name.



   .. py:method:: _on_merge_source_changed() -> None

      Rebuild one row per level of the selected column.



   .. py:method:: _on_merge_changed() -> None

      Summarize the grouping the boxes currently describe.



   .. py:method:: _build_bins_page() -> qtpy.QtWidgets.QWidget

      Cut a continuous column into labelled groups.

      The cut points are stored as explicit numbers rather than as a rule (“quartiles”): a rule
      would be recomputed against whatever rows are loaded, so the same label would mean a
      different range after a filter changed. The suggest buttons write numbers into the field,
      which you can then edit.



   .. py:method:: _numeric_columns() -> list[str]

      Columns that can be binned — base columns plus any numeric derived ones.



   .. py:method:: _categorical_columns(*, max_levels: int = 60) -> list[str]

      Columns whose levels can be merged: discrete, and few enough to lay out one row each.

      A float column is excluded — its "levels" are its values, and merging those is what the
      bins page is for. So is anything past *max_levels*: a subject id has nothing to pool.



   .. py:method:: _on_bin_source_changed() -> None

      Suggest a name from the source, mirroring ``tacsctot`` → ``tacsctot_group``.



   .. py:method:: _on_suggest_cuts(method: str, n_bins: int) -> None

      Fill the cut-point field with values derived from the source column's distribution.



   .. py:method:: _on_bins_changed(*_args) -> None

      Refresh the interval/count preview for the bin definition being edited.



   .. py:method:: columns() -> list[nvitk.stats.frame_ops.DerivedColumn]

      The configured derived columns, in application order.



   .. py:method:: _available_columns(up_to: int | None = None) -> list[str]

      Base columns plus every derived column defined before index *up_to*.



   .. py:method:: _refresh_sources() -> None

      Repopulate the transform source combo, preserving the current pick.



   .. py:method:: _refresh_list() -> None

      Redraw the list of derived columns.



   .. py:method:: _refresh_preview() -> None

      Evaluate the whole list against the frame and report the outcome.



   .. py:method:: _current_spec() -> nvitk.stats.frame_ops.DerivedColumn

      Build a :class:`DerivedColumn` from the editor form.

      :raises ValueError: If the bin cut points cannot be parsed.



   .. py:method:: _on_kind_changed() -> None

      Swap the definition page and refresh the suggested name.



   .. py:method:: _suggest_name() -> None

      Fill the name field with the conventional name while the user has not typed one.



   .. py:method:: _validate(spec: nvitk.stats.frame_ops.DerivedColumn, *, ignore_index: int | None = None) -> str

      Return why *spec* cannot be added, or ``""``.



   .. py:method:: _on_add() -> None

      Append the form's column to the list.



   .. py:method:: _on_update() -> None

      Replace the selected column with the form's definition.



   .. py:method:: _on_remove() -> None

      Drop the selected column.



   .. py:method:: _on_move(delta: int) -> None

      Move the selected column by *delta* positions (order matters: later ones may use it).



   .. py:method:: _on_select(row: int) -> None

      Load the selected column back into the editor form.



.. py:class:: SplineTermDialog(parent: qtpy.QtWidgets.QWidget | None, *, columns: Sequence[str])

   Bases: :py:obj:`qtpy.QtWidgets.QDialog`


   Build a spline or polynomial formula term.

   Curvature in a predictor does not need a different engine: a spline basis is still linear in its
   parameters, so ``bs(age_c, df=4)`` fits inside OLS, GLM and MixedLM alike and the coefficient
   table and marginal-means plot keep working. This just spares you the patsy syntax.


   .. py:attribute:: _column


   .. py:attribute:: _kind


   .. py:attribute:: _df


   .. py:attribute:: _df_label


   .. py:attribute:: _hint


   .. py:attribute:: _preview


   .. py:method:: _sync(*_args) -> None

      Update the description and the rendered term.



   .. py:method:: term() -> str

      The patsy term to insert.



.. py:class:: CovarianceTermDialog(parent: qtpy.QtWidgets.QWidget | None, *, columns: Sequence[str], visit: str = '', subject: str = '')

   Bases: :py:obj:`qtpy.QtWidgets.QDialog`


   Build an ``mmrm`` covariance term for insertion into a formula.

   The MMRM engine takes its covariance structure from the formula itself, the way R does. This
   spares you memorising the nine structure names and the ``visit | subject`` notation, and shows
   what each structure costs in parameters before you commit to it — an unstructured covariance
   over many levels needs a lot of subjects to support.


   .. py:attribute:: _structure


   .. py:attribute:: _visit


   .. py:attribute:: _subject


   .. py:attribute:: _group


   .. py:attribute:: _hint


   .. py:attribute:: _preview


   .. py:method:: _sync(*_args) -> None

      Update the structure's description and the rendered term.



   .. py:method:: term() -> str

      The covariance term to insert.
